identity.method: Exact COL26.8 dataset 316115 nameusage search for Mandrillus leucophaeus returned the single accepted species usage 3XTLF, source checklist 2144. The pinned release search registry confirms the verbatim name and authorship, rank, accepted status, and classification; every parent was then resolved by id in its pinned hierarchy registry.
identity.scope: The dossier describes the nominal accepted COL26.8 species usage 3XTLF. The biological claim is limited to one observed behavior case in a captive-born zoo group and is not generalized to wild drills or the species as a whole.

lifeStatusScope.wild: No wild-born animals were studied. The sole reported case involved a captive-born drill group at Safari Park Dvůr Králové, Czech Republic; observations were made August–October 2020.
lifeStatusScope.domesticated: Domestication has not been assessed. The observed animals were captive-born zoo residents, which is not evidence of domestication.
lifeStatusScope.fossil: Fossil occurrence has not been assessed.

Claims are paraphrased and restricted to that group and event; no figures, video, supplementary files, or third-party material are reused.

gaps: Morphology and diagnosis were not assessed in the selected behavioral observation.
One infant-death case does not assess typical reproduction, development, lifespan, or life-history variation.

claims.text: In one captive-born drill group, the mother continued post-mortem care of her infant for about two days and then consumed the corpse; no sharing with other group members was observed. This is a single zoo observation, not evidence that the behavior is typical of drills. The authors could not determine motivation or potential benefits and did not exclude a role for captivity.
claims.locator: Abstract; Methods, Study group and Behavioral observations; Results, post-mortem and post-mortem cannibalism phases; Discussion.
claims.placeTimeScope: Safari Park Dvůr Králové, Czech Republic; one captive-born group observed August–October 2020. The reported infant survived eight days after birth.
claims.lifeStatus: Captive-born zoo group; no wild-born subjects or field observations in this case.

gaps: One captive group and one infant-death event cannot establish the frequency, causes, or species-wide pattern of social and post-mortem behavior, especially in wild groups.
No phylogenetic, population-genetic, or comparative evolutionary analysis was conducted.
A single zoo group does not provide geographic occurrence or range evidence.
No fossil or paleontological evidence was assessed.
The captive behavioral observation is not a conservation assessment, population trend, or viability estimate.

reasons: One captive-group observation supports only a bounded social-behavior claim; six facets remain not-assessed and ecology is partial.
The case does not establish species-wide behavior or its motivation; no systematic multi-source review or independent expert review has been completed.
